MAJOR: `_git("show", f"{base}:{rel}", allow_fail=True)`: a missing/invalid base ref (e.g. absent `origin/develop` after fallback) silently yields `prev={}` → status not in DONE → every completed changed item counts as a fresh transition; the gate fails open and inflates the count instead of erroring.

`main()` returns exit 0 on RuntimeError in `--report` mode: if git/IO breaks, the gate is silently green (`ok:false` only visible to a consumer parsing stdout), which contradicts "fails closed" and is easily missed by CI.

Output contract changed beyond the AC (JSON report moved to stderr→stdout, extra `delivery-completeness-skip` stderr events): any existing consumer parsing the single stderr JSON line breaks; no migration note or AC covers this.

`store-registry.json` adds `"BI-TEST-*.json"` — unrelated to the AC and unexplained; depending on list semantics it either excludes real `BI-TEST-*` items from indexing or registers stray fixtures. Scope creep in a registry governing data visibility.

`id-blocks.json` jumps `reserved_up_to` 1469→1477 with a new session starting at 1477, leaving 1470–1476 unaccounted for in this block; allocation continuity isn't verifiable from the diff (risk of double-allocation if another session owns them).
MINOR: AC states `JSONDecodeError propagates`; implementation wraps it in `RuntimeError` (tests assert the wrapper) — behavior is fail-closed but deviates from the literal acceptance criterion.
`skipped` paths are emitted only as a stderr event; the primary report (`ids`/count) carries no skip count, so "the gate prints the real completion count" is only partially observable.
The `try` block also wraps `audit()`, so a non-git `RuntimeError` from audit is reported under the "git/IO failure" comment/shape — misleading diagnostics.
`allow_fail=True` on `merge-base` then falling back to unverified `origin/develop` silently changes the diff base, which can silently change which items are compared.
NIT: `_repo_root()` re-implements `_git`'s subprocess/error handling instead of reusing `_git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel", allow_fail=True)` — duplicated failure-path logic.
`functools.lru_cache` on an effectively constant value adds an import and a mutable module attribute that tests must monkeypatch around; no invalidation story.
Module docstring and function docs now describe two output channels; keep the contract in one place (docs/ENGINEERING_OPERATING_STANDARD) rather than only in the script header.
SUMMARY: Solid fail-closed path loading (escape check, malformed/non-object rejection, deleted-path skip) with meaningful regression coverage of repo-root resolution.

Top risks: fail-open `git show`/base-ref fallback can silently inflate transition counts, `--report` returns 0 when the gate cannot run, and an unexplained store-registry glob plus ID-block allocation jump widen the change beyond the AC.

Recommend tightening error propagation on the base ref, making infra failure fail the gate (or explicitly documenting the report-mode contract), and justifying/excising the registry and id-block edits before merge.
